name: NJ-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: Markets price Democratic win near certain
model.rationale: The D+27 lean, McIver's incumbency and roughly thousand-to-one fundraising edge over Bucco make a Republican upset implausible; markets also price the Democratic win at about 98%. The forecast stays near the fundamentals with a slight trim for the national environment.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or unexpected outside spending surge could narrow the margin, though not plausibly the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
New Jersey's 10th District is a heavily Democratic, urban Newark-area seat, and first-term incumbent LaMonica McIver is running for a full term after winning the special election. Republican Carmen Bucco has raised only about $2,300 and reports roughly $1,000 on hand, while McIver has raised over $2.1 million with more than $800,000 banked and modest outside support.

No public general-election polling exists for the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability around 98%. With the district's strong partisan lean and the lopsided resource gap, the seat is expected to remain comfortably Democratic in November.
